merger_name: Vets Central – Castlemaine Veterinary Clinic, Vic

targets.name: The Trustee for Berkwill Family Trust

party_page.name: The Trustee for Berkwill Family Trust

merger_description:
VC Operations (WA) Pty Ltd, together with its associated entities (collectively, **Vets Central**), proposes to acquire 100% of the business assets of Castlemaine Veterinary Clinic from Berkwill Pty Ltd as trustee for Berkwill Family Trust (the **Acquisition**).   

  

Vets Central is a veterinary group that owns and operates 88 first opinion veterinary practices across Australia and New Zealand. In Australia, Vets Central’s practices provide core and ancillary veterinary services, for household pets as well as livestock, and other exotic species. The services primarily include routine, planned, and emergency veterinary services (excluding after-hours services).   

  

Castlemaine Veterinary Clinic is full-service veterinary practice in the Castlemaine area of Victoria. The business provides a range of first opinion core and ancillary veterinary services for household pets in the local area.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between Vets Central and
Castlemaine Veterinary Clinic in the supply of veterinary
services in the Castlemaine area
b. there are alternative suppliers of veterinary services in the
Castlemaine area and more broadly at the regional, state
and national level.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
